candidates.character_or_thing: John Stewart's sentient construct of his dead sister Ellie

claim_citation.quote: John Stewart, who has resigned from the Green Lantern Corps after the United Planets seized control and ruled Earth off-limits, encounters an alien Lantern who believes John is in violation of the Corps' new rules.

candidates.summary: A partial/assisted living construct: John makes Ellie as an autonomous construct to help his mother, and later discussion indicates it becomes fully sentient/ongoing. This is one of the wildest ring uses because it crosses from simple hard-light shaping into a person-like companion.
candidates.title: Green Lantern: War Journal #1
candidates.what_visibly_happens: John manifests a child-sized green construct of his dead sister Ellie that can walk around and interact like a person.

claim_citation.quote: John constructed a green mastodonic construct of himself to fight his Kryptonian ally, pushing his boundaries to the limit.

candidates.summary: A full-body combat construct: John makes a gigantic version of himself to throw hands with Superman. This is a direct, visible oversized battle-avatar rather than a tool or weapon.
candidates.title: Green Lantern: 10 Coolest Constructs John Stewart Ever Made, Ranked
candidates.what_visibly_happens: He forms a huge green duplicate of himself and uses it to fight Superman.

candidates.character_or_thing: John Stewart's construct holding Earth together

claim_citation.quote: He used his ring to keep the earth from getting sucked into the sun by its gravity.

candidates.summary: A planetary-scale support construct: John uses the ring to stabilize Earth against catastrophic gravity. This is temporary but physically enormous, with the ring acting like a structural patch job for an entire planet.
candidates.title: Green Lantern: 10 Coolest Constructs John Stewart Ever Made, Ranked
candidates.what_visibly_happens: He creates construct support that keeps Earth from being pulled into the sun.

candidates.character_or_thing: John Stewart's monster and army of demons

claim_citation.quote: In a mind-blowing battle, the former Green Lantern mustered up a giant monster and an army of demons to defeat the protectors of Earth without losing control over his constructs.

candidates.summary: A full combat scene featuring multiple large constructs. This is more extreme than a single weapon because John generates both a monster and a whole demon army under ultraviolet influence.
candidates.title: Green Lantern: 10 Coolest Constructs John Stewart Ever Made, Ranked
candidates.what_visibly_happens: He manifests a giant monster plus a swarm/army of demon constructs.

claim_citation.quote: John Stewart decided to build a sniper rifle construct that was so precise and deadly that it only took one shot to thwart the threat from such a long distance.

candidates.series_issue_year: Green Lantern Corps Special #1, Vol. 1 (year not provided in retrieved source)
candidates.summary: A partial/functional weapon construct: John builds a precision rifle to solve an impossible long-range kill shot. This is one of his signature architect-minded constructs because it is both detailed and lethal.
candidates.title: Green Lantern: 10 Coolest Constructs John Stewart Ever Made, Ranked
candidates.what_visibly_happens: He creates a fully formed sniper rifle and fires from extreme distance to hit Bedovian.

candidates.character_or_thing: John Stewart's recreated solar system construct

claim_citation.quote: Fueled by his regret, he was able to temporarily manifest the entire system as a construct in the hopes of bringing it back again.

candidates.summary: A massive temporary reconstruction: John tries to manifest an entire solar system after causing a catastrophic loss. This is one of the most insane scale feats in the retrieved material, but the source frames it as temporary and ultimately unsuccessful.
candidates.title: Green Lantern: 10 Coolest Constructs John Stewart Ever Made, Ranked
candidates.what_visibly_happens: He briefly creates an entire solar system-sized construct out of regret.

claim_citation.quote: Zod claims it would take weeks to construct such a device since it was lost to the ages, but Stewart proved him otherwise by building it in mere minutes using his ring.

candidates.summary: A highly technical assisted construct: John rapidly builds an ancient alien device from blueprints. This is not the biggest construct by size, but it is one of the most insane because of the speed and precision.
candidates.title: Green Lantern: 10 Coolest Constructs John Stewart Ever Made, Ranked
candidates.what_visibly_happens: He assembles a complex alien tele-disruptor almost instantly from Zod's plans.

claim_citation.quote: That’s right, John was able to create pure Kryptonite down to the last isotope using his sheer willpower.

candidates.summary: A molecular-level construct/materialization: John creates Kryptonite itself, not just a weapon using it. This is one of the most extreme examples of ring precision in the retrieved set.
candidates.title: Green Lantern: 10 Coolest Constructs John Stewart Ever Made, Ranked
candidates.what_visibly_happens: He manifests Kryptonite material down to isotope-level detail.

candidates.character_or_thing: John Stewart's army of Marine constructs

claim_citation.quote: He relied on the power of his ring by creating a formidable armada of marines.

candidates.series_issue_year: Green Lantern Vol. 4 #49 (year not provided in retrieved source)
candidates.summary: A full-army construct: John creates and remotely pilots a squad/armada of Marines, including their weapons and ammunition. This is a partial construct only in the sense that it mimics human combatants; visually it is a whole battlefield force.
candidates.title: Green Lantern: 10 Coolest Constructs John Stewart Ever Made, Ranked
candidates.what_visibly_happens: He conjures a whole Marine army and controls their firing in battle.
